title: tool invoke gatekeeper and schema-fallback adapter for streaming compatibility
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Streaming tool/function invocations from OpenAI-style clients sometimes emit partial fragments, non-conforming JSON, or out-of-band metadata. Upstream services expect a coherent tool invocation envelope, and our openai-compat layer needs to be resilient without requiring client changes. This PR introduces a lightweight runtime adapter ("Gatekeeper") that sits in the invoke path and performs three responsibilities in a backwards-compatible way: 1) resilient fragment coalescing and streaming admission control, 2) schema fallback and heuristic mapping for non-conforming tool payloads, and 3) structured-output annotations (schema_confidence, fragment_repaired) for downstream telemetry and gradual rollouts.

What this changes: The Gatekeeper adapts incoming streaming fragments into a consistent internal invoke envelope. It performs incremental validation: if fragments form valid JSON, pass-through is used; if fragments are invalid but repairable (common cases: trailing commas, isolated escaped newlines, missing closing brace), Gatekeeper attempts a deterministic repair and tags the envelope with schema_confidence and fragment_repaired=true. If a tool signature does not match any registered tool schema, Gatekeeper applies heuristic mapping rules (name alias table + type inference) and attaches a best_match_tool and confidence level. All repairs/mappings are recorded as events to observability and appear in trace spans. A feature flag toolcall_adapter_v2 controls rollout.

Compatibility & safety: No upstream API changes. Clients that already send well-formed tool calls are unchanged. The adapter rejects clearly invalid/ambiguous streams with a 400 and a structured error payload to keep behavior explicit for integrators. Repair heuristics are conservative and logged; a follow-up PR will add an operator console to flip strict mode per tenant.

Testing and verification: Unit tests cover edge fragments, near-miss JSON, alias resolution, and concurrent streaming sessions. End-to-end golden tests simulate chunked streams from the OpenAI SDKs and assert final invoke envelope parity with expected tool schema variants. CI includes a newly added flaky test harness that runs streaming scenarios under jitter.

Rollout plan: Enable toolcall_adapter_v2 as an opt-in feature for 10% of traffic in Dedicated, monitor metrics (toolcall.fragment_repaired, toolcall.schema_mismatch, toolcall.reject_rate, p95_infer_latency), then widen to 50% before global default. We will measure customer-facing error rate and a small latency delta due to admission processing; batching heuristics are preserved.

Notes: This PR also adds cross-cutting telemetry tags to help correlate repairs with prompt fingerprints and model variant. See docs/openai-toolcall-compat.md for operator-facing descriptions and migration guidance.

review_comments: Riley: please document the exact repair rules and where we should stop trying to auto-fix (edge cases like ambiguous bracket counts). Also add a metric for repaired_count/attempted_count.
Maya (author): added detailed repair rules to docs and a gatekeeper.repair_attempts metric; left an owner TODO for the operator console work.
Samir: can we avoid copying large buffers for every fragment? Suggest switch to slice-backed buffers and limit max_buffer_size per session.
Maya: switched to slice-backed buffer and added a safeguard with max_buffer_size configured per tenant; tests updated.
Elena: tests look good but add a deterministic seed for jitter in e2e harness to reduce flakiness.
Maya: added deterministic jitter seed and re-ran e2e; CI green.
QA: flagged unexpected behavior when tool name matches multiple aliases; clarified fallback order and added an explicit tie-breaker rule.
ci_log: Initial CI: lint failed (golangci: formatting on gatekeeper.go). Fix applied. Re-ran: all checks passed (unit, e2e, integration streaming). Flaky harness ran 3x, 0 failures.
release_notes: Introduce a streaming tool-invoke adapter (Gatekeeper) that coalesces fragments, applies conservative schema repair, and writes schema_confidence telemetry. Rollout guarded by feature flag toolcall_adapter_v2. No client changes required.
